quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: How should you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you are moving. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads divided by a median. Stay to the right.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you speed up before the turn.
When traffic on that street moves to the right.
When traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left, if there is no sign prohibiting it. Do not turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and the shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and the shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part gives you much less protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle the lap belt.

questions.question: You have a green light, but traffic blocks the intersection ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
Follow other vehicles into the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking it. If you enter and the light turns red, you will block other traffic. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has bright lights on and you cannot see well. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at bright oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other car from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop if cars are coming.
Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Go through the intersection slowly, not always stopping.
Stop only if traffic is on the side roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a complete stop. Let vehicles and pedestrians cross safely, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What affects how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars cannot be seen or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Areas where cars have enough space behind the truck.
Areas where cars are several car lengths from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars cannot be seen or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars are not visible to the driver or are too close. These areas make it hard for the truck driver to stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: When a bicyclist makes a left turn, what can they do?

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Do not be surprised to see a bicyclist in the left lane when turning left.

questions.question: A driver may park in a space reserved for people with disabilities if the vehicle displays the proper license plates:

options.text: No matter who is in the vehicle.
Only if the driver is disabled.
And the disabled person named on the registration is in the vehicle.
If someone in the driver's immediate family is disabled.

questions.correctAnswerText: And the disabled person named on the registration is in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: To park in a disability-reserved space, the vehicle must be transporting the specific disabled person named on the registration or permit.

questions.question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the proper lane to turn, drive to the next intersection and turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your emergency signals or horn when needed.

questions.question: When you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Stop before crossing the intersection.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down, look for cross traffic, and go carefully.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal blood alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment is necessary to react correctly to what you see or hear while driving. Any amount of alcohol can reduce your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road widens ahead.
The right lane ends soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
The left lane ends soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs indicate:

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing downward is always a yield sign. Be ready to slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: If your car's suspension is bad, it can cause:

options.text: Vehicle control problems.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicle control problems.
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride on different road surfaces. If your vehicle bounces too much after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the speed of traffic, signal, and:

options.text: Expect other traffic to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Before merging onto the interstate, find a gap, speed up to match traffic, and signal. Merge into the gap when it is safe. Watch other traffic closely and do not assume other drivers will make room for you.
